means.en: Belonging to the Sindhu-Sarasvati civilisation, also called the Indus Valley Civilisation or the Harappan Civilisation.
The script on Harappan seals and pottery. It has not been deciphered, so nobody can read it yet.
A tool, pot, bead or other object made by humans. Artefacts are the main source for the time before writing.
To work out what an unknown script says. The script has then been deciphered.
The preserved remains, traces or impressions of plants, animals or humans from the distant past.
human
upright
An ancestor that walked on two legs, made handaxes and cleavers, and was the first hominin to leave Africa, around 2 million years ago.
human
handy
An early human ancestor of Africa, known from Olduvai Gorge. It made simple chopper tools.
Homo neanderthalensis lived in Europe and southwest Asia until about 40,000 years ago and made Middle Palaeolithic flake tools.
The area of the oldest human settlements: Africa, Asia and Europe together.
southern
primate
An early ancestor from before Homo habilis. The book calls these our early ancestors.
A group that includes modern humans and our early human-like ancestors, known as toolmakers.

plain.en: a warmer time between ice ages

means.en: between
of ice
A warmer time when the ice drew back. In these times the Sahara and Arabia were wetter than they are now.
copper
stone
The age when people used copper along with stone tools.
middle
stone
The stage between hunting-gathering and farming, marked by tiny stone tools called microliths.
new
stone
The stage when people began farming, settled in villages, kept animals and used polished stone tools.
old
stone
The first and longest stage of the Stone Age, when people lived by hunting and gathering and used simple stone tools.

plain.en: the soft food inside a bone

means.en: The soft, protein-rich food inside large animal bones.
small
stone
A very small stone tool, often fixed in a handle with others.
A weapon sent through the air, such as a spear or an arrow, often tipped with a sharp point.
Food or goods beyond what people need at once. The book says surplus laid the foundation for civilisation.
A pointed stone tool used to engrave marks on bones and shells.
A powder that gives colour. Early people used it for paint and to decorate their bodies.
Using signs, marks and pictures to pass on an idea to other people.
A smooth, ground stone blade, used for work such as clearing trees.

plain.en: bringing a plant or animal under human control

means.en: People choose which plants and animals to raise, and over time this produces new breeds.
The care and breeding of farm animals.
A large stone with a hollow in its top. A smaller hand-stone is rubbed over grain on it to make flour.
Living in one place all year instead of moving from camp to camp.
A red or orange semi-precious stone used for beads.
A building or set of bins for storing grain.
A blue semi-precious stone used for beads.
A kind of Indian cattle with a hump on its shoulders.
Alluvial soil is the fine soil a river leaves behind. It is good for farming.

plain.en: a line cut by a plough

means.en: The long, narrow line a plough leaves in the soil.
A low dam across a small stream, built to hold water for fields. Early Harappans built them in the foothills of Baluchistan.

plain.en: an age measured in a laboratory

means.en: A way of finding the age of old plant or bone material from the carbon left in it.

plain.en: curved belt of good farmland in West Asia

means.en: The crescent-shaped foothills of the Zagros and Taurus, from the Mediterranean to the Persian Gulf.

plain.en: a city that rules itself and the land around it

means.en: A sovereign state centred on a city that rules the surrounding land.

plain.en: many regions ruled by one family

means.en: A dynasty is a family of rulers. The book calls the Akkadian empire the first of these.

plain.en: bringing water to crops by human work

means.en: Leading water to fields through canals, instead of waiting for rain.
A sovereign state makes its own decisions.

plain.en: the place where wealth is kept

means.en: The store of a city's or a ruler's wealth.
A tower-like stepped temple with several floors and the main temple at the top. It also served as the city's treasury.
A trading place in the Persian Gulf named in Sargon's tablets.
They built a powerful empire in today's Turkey, around the second millennium BCE.
A trading place on the Persian Gulf named in Sargon's tablets.

plain.en: a trading land named on Mesopotamian tablets

means.en: It is generally identified with the Sindhu-Sarasvati civilisation.
cuneus is Latin for wedge. Sumerian scribes pressed a cut reed into damp clay to make these marks.
Someone whose work was writing. Few people could write, so scribes had a high status.
An upright stone with carving or writing on it, set up for people to see.
The cut reed a scribe pressed into clay.
The Egyptians' own name for their land, after the black soil of the river valley.

plain.en: the picture signs of Egyptian writing

means.en: hieros means holy and glyph means carving. Some signs stand for sounds, and some for whole words.
The rising of the Nile over its plain each year, and the season named after it.

plain.en: early paper made from a plant

means.en: Strips of the papyrus plant were laid criss-cross, pressed, dried and polished into sheets.
The title of the rulers of ancient Egypt, who were treated as gods on earth.
Egyptians believed each person's ka lived on after death if the body was preserved.
Mastaba means bench in Arabic. It was a rectangular structure placed over a burial chamber.
Organs were removed, the body was dried with natron, oiled and wrapped in linen.
Embalmers used it to dry the body during mummification.

plain.en: a farm worker tied to the land

means.en: A worker who farms land owned by someone else and cannot freely leave it.
An instrument shaken at Egyptian festivals and ceremonies.

plain.en: a person who asks the spirits questions

means.en: In Shang China, diviners prepared the bones and read the cracks. Kings often read them too.

plain.en: a line of rulers from one family

means.en: China's history is organised by dynasties: Shang, Zhou, Qin and Han in this chapter.
Soil of very fine, wind-blown dust. It covers much of the land around the Huang He, which gives the Yellow River its colour.

plain.en: a sign for a whole word

means.en: logo means word and graph means writing. A logograph stands for a word or a morpheme, and not for a single sound.

plain.en: the smallest piece of language with a meaning

means.en: The word unkind has two morphemes: un and kind.

plain.en: a bone used to ask the spirits a question

means.en: An ox shoulder blade or tortoise shell, heated until it cracked. People read the cracks as an answer. An oracle is an answer believed to come from a god or a spirit.

plain.en: a thing that shows high rank

means.en: An object people own to show who they are, such as carved jade in early China.

plain.en: the belief that heaven chooses a ruler

means.en: Zhou rulers were believed to be appointed by heaven, but a ruler could be dismissed when his people did not prosper.

plain.en: a group of traders travelling together

means.en: Traders crossed deserts in groups, with their animals and goods, for safety.

plain.en: moving from place to place with herds

means.en: Nomadic people have no fixed village. They move with their animals to find grass and water.
A building material made by packing damp soil into a frame, layer by layer. Many older walls in China are built this way.
Tangible evidence is a real object, such as a seal or a weight found in a dig.
A thin chip of stone struck off a larger stone. Some tools were made from flakes.
A place on the ground where people made a fire.
Writing cut or pressed into a hard surface such as stone, clay or metal.
A stone tool shaped to a point on both faces, used for cutting.
A stone tool with a broad, straight edge, used for chopping and splitting.
A heavy stone tool with one rough cutting edge.
A food plant that grows under the ground.
A barbed spear used to catch fish.
A curved blade used to cut grain and wild grass.
Animals kept by people on farms, such as cattle, sheep and goats.
Growing plants on purpose, by preparing the soil and sowing seed.
Land changed by fields and farm work.
